9 trades this week. My 2 biggest losses came from stops that slipped.

Paper account, Monday to Thursday: 7 trades, 4 wins, 3 losses, +$4,825.
Evaluation account, Friday: 2 trades, 1 win, 1 loss, -$250.
2 ES on every trade, before commissions.

My best 2 trades had the stop and the target set before entry, and I left them alone. +$1,625 and +$2,850.

My worst 2 were planned as 4 point losses. Fast moves pushed the fills to 6.25 and 5 points.

Next week I size for that slip, not for the perfect fill.

Save this for the week your stop doesn't fill where you put it.

fb:
This week my paper account made $4,825 and my evaluation account lost $250, before commissions. Here's every trade.

Monday through Thursday I traded my paper account. Monday a stop-out cost $400, then a short paid $850. Tuesday a long stopped me for -$375, and a short ran to its target for +$1,625. Wednesday I didn't trade. Thursday was 3 longs: +$900, then -$625 on a rushed second entry, then a patient entry that reached its target for +$2,850. That's +$4,825 on 7 trades.

Friday was my evaluation account. My first short had a 4 point mental stop, and a fast spike filled me at 5 points, -$500. The second short was up $1,275 at its best, came back toward my entry, and I closed it for +$250. Day: -$250.

Every trade was 2 ES with the risk decided before I clicked. The two stops that slipped are why next week's size leaves room for a worse fill.

I work a full-time job and trade around it. Weeks like this are why I decide the loss first and let the chart decide the rest.

Share this with a trader who mixes practice results and evaluation results in the same column.
